title: BIO-123-Notes
text:
Cell theory:

Cells are the fundamental units of life.
All living organisms are composed of cells.
All cells come from preexisting cells.
Modern cells evolved from a common ancestor.

3 important implications of cell theory:

Studying cell biology is in some sense the same as studying life.
Life is continuous.
The origin of life on Earth was marked by the origin of the first cells.

several important roles of membrane:

acts as a selectively permeable barrier:

prevent some substances from crossing in
permit other substances to enter & leave the cell

regulate transport across it \(\Rightarrow\) allows the cell to maintain a more or less constant internal environment
important in

communicating with adjacent cells
receiving signals from the environment


Everything inside the cell, except for the nucleus if the cell has one, is termed the cytoplasm.
The cytosol is the fluid cytoplasm not contained inside another compartment.
prokaryote: organisms in Archaea and Bacteria

does not have membrane-enclosed internal compartments
does not have a nucleus

eukaryote: protists 原生生物, plants, fungi, and animals

contain membrane-enclosed comaprtments called organelles

nucleus:

where most of the cell’s DNA is located
where gene expression begins






nucleoid [病毒] 病毒核心; [细胞] 类核: region in the cell where the DNA is located
ribosomes 核糖体: complexes of RNA and proteins in the cytoplasm
cell wall

located outside the cell membrane
supports the cell
determines cells’ shape

cell wall of most bacteria, but not archaea:

contain peptidoglycan: a polymer of amino sugars that is linked at regular intervals to short peptides

in some bacteria, outer membrane: polysaccharide-rich phospholipid membrane

encloses the peptidoglycan layer

in some bacteria. capsule: a slimy layer composed mostly of polysaccharides

enclosing the cell wall

some bacteria have an internal membrane system: contains molecules needed for photosynthesis
some prokaryotes swim by using appendages called flagella

sometimes look like tiny corkscrews

pill: structures made of protein

project from the surfaces of some types of bacterial cells

cytoskeleton: protein filaments

play roles in cell division, cell movement, and in maintaining the shapes of cells.






nucleus:

location of most of the cell’s DNA and the site of DNA replication
the site where gene transcription is turned on or off
nucleolus: a region within the nucleus

where ribosomes begin to be assembled from RNA and proteins


the nucleus is enclosed by nuclear envelope: an integrated structure composed of two membranes
chromosomes: long, thin threads

made up by chromatin: inside nucleus, DNA molecule + proteins

endomembrane system: interconnected system of membrane-enclosed compartments, includes:

cell membrane
nuclear envelope
endoplasmic reticulum 内质网
Golgi apparatus [细胞] 高尔基氏体; 内网器
lysosomes 溶酶体

vesicles 囊: membrane-surrounded droplets

shuttle substances between the various components of the endomembrane system

endoplasmic reticulum (ER) 内质网: networks of interconnected membranes branching throughout the cytoplasm

forming tubes and flattened sacs

rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) 带有核糖体的内质网: many ribosomes attached to the outer surface of the membrane, giving it a “rough” appearance in electron microscopy

receives into its lumen 内腔 (管状器官内的空腔) certain newly synthesized proteins

segregating them away from the cytoplasm
participates in transporting these proteins to other locations in the cell

proteins can be

chemically modified to alter their functions
“tag” them for delivery to specific cellular destinations

proteins are sent to destinations elsewhere in the cell enclosed within vesicles that pinch off from the RER
most membrane-bound proteins are made in the RER
glycoproteins 糖蛋白: some proteins become covalently linked to carbohydrate groups in the RER

smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) 平滑内质网: lacks ribosomes and is more tubular (and less like fattened sacs) than the RER, but shows continuity with portions of the RER

responsible for the chemical modification of small molecules taken in by the cell that may be toxic to the cell

make the targeted molecules more polar, so they are more water soluble and easily removed

is the site for glycogen degradation in animal cells
where lipids and steroids are synthesized, as well as some polysaccharides 多糖 in plant cells
store calcium ions, released trigger numerous cell responses

Golgi apparatus 内网器, consists of two components: flattened membranous sacs called cisternae 潴泡 (singular cisterna) that are piled up like saucers, and small membrane-enclosed vesicles

receives protein-containing vesicles from the RER
modifies, concentrates, packages, and sorts proteins. before they are sent to their cellular or extracellular destinations
adds carbohydrates to proteins
modifies other carbohydrates that were attached to proteins in the RER
where some polysaccharides for the plant cell wall are synthesized
cuts certain large precursor proteins transferred from the RER into smaller, functional fragments

3 functionally distinct regions (faces) of Golgi apparatus:

The cis face lies nearest to the nucleus or a patch of RER
The trans face lies closest to the cell membrane
The medial face lies in between

primary lysosomes: originate from the Golgi apoparatus
contain digestive enzymes
the sites where macromolecules (protein, polysaccharides, nucleic acids, lipids) are hydrolyzed into their monomers
phagocytosis 吞噬作用: a process of food, other cells, or foreign objects enter the cell
secondary lysosome [细胞][免疫] 次级溶酶体: phagosome 吞噬体 fuses with a primary lysosome to form a ~

where digestion occurs
there reactions are enhanced by the acidity of the lysosome’s interior

exocytosis (细胞生物学) 胞吐作用:

the “used” secondary lysosome containing undigested particles
moves to the cell membrane
fuses with it, and releases the undigested contents to the environment

autophagy (生物学) 自噬: programmed destruction of cell components

some cell components are continually being broken down and replaced by new ones

lysosomes 溶酶体:

where the cell breaks down its own materials
with the proper signal, lysosomes can engulf entire organelles, hydrolyzing their constituents

lysosomal storage diseases: caused by the failure of lysosomes to digest specific cellular components

invariably harmful or fatal
e.g. Tay-Sachs disease 黑蒙性家族性痴愚; 泰-萨二氏病

a particular lipid called a ganglioside [生化] 神经节苷脂 is not broken down in the lysosomes
instead accumulates in brain cells
a baby starts exhibiting neurological symptoms and becomes blind, deaf, and unable to swallow after 6 months of age
death occurs before age 4


plant cells do not appear to contain lysosomes, but the vacuole [细胞] 液泡 of a plant cell may function in an equivalent capacity because it, like lysosomes, hydrolyzes macromolecules
energy is harvested from

fuel molecules in the mitochondria 线粒体 (mitochondrion 的复数)

found in all eukaryotic cells

sunlight in the chloroplasts 叶绿体 of plant cells\

energy in biological systems is stored and transferred in the form of covalent bonds in organic molecules
In eukaryotic cells, breakdown of energy-rich molecules sucha s glucose begins in the cytoplasm.
mitochondria:

harvests the chemical-bond energy of those molecules in a form that he cell can use
namely the energy-rich molecule ATP (adenosine triphosphate 腺苷三磷酸)
some can reproduce and divide independently of the central nucleus
Cells that are active in movement and growth require the most chemical-bond energy and tend to have the most mitochondria.

cellular respiration

production of ATP in the mitochondria
using fuel molecules and molecular oxygen (\(\ce{O2}\))

Mitochondria have two membranes:

outer membrane:

smooth
permits the movement of substances into and out of the organelle

inner membrane:

folds inward in many places
has a surface area much greater tha nthat of the outer membrane
cristae 脊: shelflike structures
exerts much more control over what enters and leaves the space it encloses than does the outer membrane

large protein complexes embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane

participate tin cellular respiration


mitochondrial matrix 线粒体基质

the space enclosed by the inner membrane
contains ribosomes and DNA that are used to make some of the mitochondrial proteins needed for cellular respiration

plastids 质体，色素体:

occur only in the cells of plants and certain protists
can divide independently of the cell nucleus

chloroplasts 叶绿体: \(\nwarrow\) (one type of plastids)

contain the green pigment chlorophyll 叶绿素
are the sites of photosynthesis

light energy is converted into chemical-bond energy

enclosed by two membranes
thylakoids 类囊体: a series of internal membrane that often look like stacks of flat, hollow pita bread

only 10% are phospholipids 磷脂
the rest are galactose-substituted diglycerides 半乳糖取代的二甘油酯 and sulfolipids 硫脂
are the most abundant lipids in the biosphere
the membranes of the thylakoids contain chlorophyll and other pigments taht harvest light energy for photosynthesis

The thylakoids of one granum may be connected to those of other grana, making the interior of the chloroplast a highly developed network, much like the ER.
stroma 间质: the fluid in which the grana are suspended

contains ribosomes nad DNA

used to synthasize some chloroplast polypeptides



chromoplast 色素母细胞 (another type of plastids)

make and store red, yellow, and orange pigments
especially in flowers and fruits

leucoplasts [植] 白色体 (another type of plastids):

storage organelles that store starch

3 other organelles whose boundary membranes separate their specialized chemical reactions and contents from the rest fo the cytoplasm: peroxisomes 过氧物酶体, glyoxysomes 糖体, and vacuoles 液泡.
peroxisome 过氧物酶体:

found only in plants
organelles that accumulate toxic peroxides

e.g. hydrogen peroxide (\(\ce{H2O2}\)): occur as byproducts of some biochemical reactions
safely broken down inside the peroxisomes without mixing with other parts of the cell
\[\ce{RH2 + O2 -> R + H2O2 \text{(cellular reactions)}} \\
\ce{2H2O2 -> 2H2O + O2 \text{(inside peroxisome)}}\]


glyoxysome 糖体:

found only in plants
most abundant in young plants
they are the locations where stored lipids are converted into carbohydrates for transport to growing cells
The direct conversion of fat to carbohydrate is unique to these plants.

vacuole 液泡:

occur in many eukaryotic cells but particularly those of plants, fungi, and protists
arise from the ER or Golgi apparatus
structure:

in many plant cells, ~ take up more than 90% of the cell volume
grow as the cell grows
presence of dissolved substances in the vacuole causes water to enter it from the cytosol, making the vacuole swell like a balloon
A mature plant cell does not swell when the vacuole fills with water, since it has a rigid cell wall.
Instead, it stiffens 绷紧 from the increase in water pressure (called turgor (细胞组织的) 肿胀), and this supports the plant body.

reproduction:

~ contains some fo the pigments (especially blue and pink) in the petals and fruits of flowering plants
these pigments – the anthocyanins 花色素苷 – are visual cues that help attract animals that assist in pollination or seed dispersal

digestion:

in some plants, ~ in seeds contain molecules that hydrolyze stored proteins into monomers
during seed germination 发芽, the monomers are used as food by the developing plant seedlings

storage:

storing water
store toxic molecules and waste products
they may be poisonous or distasteful, these stored materials deter some animals from eating the plants and contribute to plant defense and survival
e.g. tannins 单宁酸: a class of polyphenols 多元酚 (具有抗氧化作用), made in many plants; in tea and red wine

bitter taste deters predators
dark color acts like animal melanin 黑色素 to protect the plant from ultraviolet light dmg
made in the chloroplast and end up in the vacuole
A newly disc9overed organelle, named tannosome 单宁体, contains tannins.



cytoskeleton 细胞骨架:

supports the cell and maintains its shape
holds cell organelles and other particles in position within the cell
moves organelles and other particles around in the cell
involved with movements of the cytoplasm, called cytoplasmic streaming 细胞质流动
interacts with extracellular structures, helping anchor 锚 the cell in place

microfilaments 微丝:

can exist as single filaments, in bundles, or in networks
about \(\pu{7nm}\) in diameter and up to several micrometers long
two major roles:

helpo the entire cell or parts of the cell move
determine and stabilize cell shape

assembled from monomers of actin 肌动蛋白: a protein that exists in several forms; has many function, especially in animals

has distinct ends: designated “plus” and “minus”
these ends permit actin monomers to interact with one another to form long, double-helical chains
the polymerization of actin into microfilaments is reversible
the microfilaments can disappear from cells by breaking down into monomers of free actin
Special actin-binding proteins mediate these processes.
in non-muscle cells, ~ filaments are associated with localized changes in cell shape

e.g. cytoplasmic streaming: flowing movement of the cytoplasm
e.g. amoeboid movement [细胞] 变形运动
e.g. “pinching” contractions that divide an animal cell into two daughter cells

involved in the formation of cellular extensions called pseudopodia 伪足: enables some cells to move


intermediate filaments 中间纤维

at least 50 different kinds
generally fall into six molecular classes that share the same general structure
one of these classes consists of fibrous proteins fo the keratin family, which also includes the proteins that make up hair and fingernails
tough, ropelike protein structures \(\pu{8-12nm}\) in diametere
more permanet tthatn the other two types in that they do not continually form and re-form
two major structural functions:

anchor cell structures in place

radiate from the nuclear envelope and help maintain the position of the nucleus and other organelles in the cell

resist tension

maintian rigidity in body surface tissues by stretching through the cytoplasm
connecting specialized membrane structures called desmosomes 细胞桥粒 (上皮细胞膜中的局部增厚部份)



microtubules 微管: long, hollow, unbranched cylinders about \(\pu{25nm}\) in diameter and up to several micrometers long

two roles in the cell:

form a rigid internal skeleton for some cells
act as a framework along which motor proteins can move structures within the cell

Microtubule = chain of dimers
dimer 二聚物 = \(\alpha\)-tubulin 微管蛋白 + \(\beta\)-tubulin (paired)
\(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) = two similar proteins
One dimer → next dimer → tube grows
Thirteen chains of tubulin doublets surround the central cavity of hte microtubule.
\[\ce{\alpha-tubulin + \beta-tubulin -> \alpha\beta doublet -> polymer of doublets (microtubule)}\]
the two ends of a microtubule are different: one is designated the “plus” end and the other the “minus” end.
Tubulin dimers can be rapidly added or subtracted, mainly at the plus end, lengthening or shortening the microtubule.
\[\text{Microtubules} \leftrightarrow \text{tubulin doublets}\]
The capacity to change length rapidly makes microtubules dynamic structures: they are readily adapted for new purposes in the cell.
e.g. by disassembly 分解 and reassembly 重组, they can drag along substances attached to them
In plants, microtubules act as a framework for the assembly of cellulose and help orient the cellulose fibers of the cell wall.

motor proteins: specialized molecules that use cellular energy to change their shapes and move

bind to and move along the microtubules, carrying materials from one part of the cell to another
two main types of motor proteins:

kinesins 驱动蛋白: move materials toward the “plus” end
dyneins 动力蛋白: move materials toward the “minus” end


microtubules and their associated proteins line the interior of cilia 纤毛 and flagella 鞭毛 on eukaryotic cells

many cells have one or the other of these appendages, which form from projections of the cell membrane

cilia: \(\pu{0.25\mu m}\) in length

They occur by the hundreds on individual cells and move stiffly to either propel the cell (i.e. in protists 原生生物) or to move fluid over a stationary cell (i.e. in the human respiratory system)

flagella: longer, \(\pu{100}\) to \(\pu{200\mu m}\)

occur singly or in pairs
can push or pull a cell through its aqueous environment

In cell biology, two approaches are often used to show that a structure or process A causes function B:

Inhibition: Use a drug thta inhibits A and see if B still occurs. If it does not, then A is probably a causative factor for B.
Mutation: Examine a cell that lacks the gene (or genes) for A and see if B still occurs. If it does not, then A is probably a causative factor for B.







3 major roles of plant cell wall

provides support for the cell and plant by remaining rigid

flexible enough that it can allow the plant to bend in the wind

acts as a barrier to infection by fungi and other organisms that can cause plant diseases
contributes to plant form by growing as the plant cells expand

Cytoplasms of adjacent plant cells are connected by numerous cell membrane-lined channels called plasmodesmata (plasmodesma) 胞间连丝, about \(\pu{20-40\mu m}\)



Many animal cells are surrounded by, or in contact with an extracellular matrix 细胞外基质.

细胞外基质：由特定类型的细胞产生但不是细胞的部分：为细胞提供支持并常作为组织的共同成分之一，尤其是结缔组织。

This matrix is composed of three types of molecules:

fibrous proteins such as collagen 胶原质

collagen: the most abundant protein in mammals, constituting over 25% of the protein in the human body

a matrix of glycoproteins 糖蛋白 termed proteoglycans 蛋白聚糖, consisting primarily of sugars
a third group of proteins that link the fibrous proteins and the gel-like proteoglycan matrix together

Several functions of extracellular matrix:

holds cells together in tissues
contributes to the physical properties of cellular aggregates called tissues

Cartilage 软骨 and bone are part of connective tissue.
e.g. The mineral component of bone is laid down on an organized extracellular matix.

In tissue engineering, cells are removed from the extracellular matrix and the latter serves as a scaffold for the development of new organs with the correct architecture.


helps filter materials passing between different tissues

e.g. especially important in the kidney

helps orient cell movements during embryonic development and during tissue repair
plays a role in chemical signaling from one cell to another

Proteins connect the cell’s cell membrane to the extracellular matrix.
These proteins (e.g. integrin 整合蛋白) span the cell membrane and are involved with transmitting signals to the interior of the cell.
This allows communication between the extracellular matrix and the cytoplasm of the cell.






The first life on Earth was prokaryotic.

Prokaryotes are simple cells without a nucleus, like bacteria.

For about 1 billion years, only prokaryotes existed on Earth.
This period started when prokaryotic cells first appeared.
It lasted until about 2.7 billion years ago.
At 2.7 billion years ago, the first evidence of eukaryotic cells appears in ancient rocks.

Eukaryotes are complex cells with a nucleus – the ancestors of plants and animals.

A single prokaryotic cell is often biochemically specialized, limited in the resources it can use and the functions it can perform.


theory: the endomembrane system and the cell nucleus originated by related processes
A bacterium with enclosed compartments would have several evolutionary advantages.
Chemicals could be concentrated in particular regions of the cell, allowing chemical reactions to proceed more efficiently.
A biochemical process could be segregated within an organelle with, for example, a different pH from the rest of the cell, creating more favorable conditions for that process.
DNA transcription could be separated from translation, providing more opportunities for separate control of these steps in gene expression.



Symbiosis 共生 means “living together,” and often refers to two organisms that coexist, each one supplying something that the other needs.

text:
3 major roles of plant cell wall

provides support for the cell and plant by remaining rigid

flexible enough that it can allow the plant to bend in the wind

acts as a barrier to infection by fungi and other organisms that can cause plant diseases
contributes to plant form by growing as the plant cells expand

Cytoplasms of adjacent plant cells are connected by numerous cell membrane-lined channels called plasmodesmata (plasmodesma) 胞间连丝, about \(\pu{20-40\mu m}\)



Many animal cells are surrounded by, or in contact with an extracellular matrix 细胞外基质.

细胞外基质：由特定类型的细胞产生但不是细胞的部分：为细胞提供支持并常作为组织的共同成分之一，尤其是结缔组织。

This matrix is composed of three types of molecules:

fibrous proteins such as collagen 胶原质

collagen: the most abundant protein in mammals, constituting over 25% of the protein in the human body

a matrix of glycoproteins 糖蛋白 termed proteoglycans 蛋白聚糖, consisting primarily of sugars
a third group of proteins that link the fibrous proteins and the gel-like proteoglycan matrix together

Several functions of extracellular matrix:

holds cells together in tissues
contributes to the physical properties of cellular aggregates called tissues

Cartilage 软骨 and bone are part of connective tissue.
e.g. The mineral component of bone is laid down on an organized extracellular matix.

In tissue engineering, cells are removed from the extracellular matrix and the latter serves as a scaffold for the development of new organs with the correct architecture.


helps filter materials passing between different tissues

e.g. especially important in the kidney

helps orient cell movements during embryonic development and during tissue repair
plays a role in chemical signaling from one cell to another

Proteins connect the cell’s cell membrane to the extracellular matrix.
These proteins (e.g. integrin 整合蛋白) span the cell membrane and are involved with transmitting signals to the interior of the cell.
This allows communication between the extracellular matrix and the cytoplasm of the cell.

title: Chapter 5 Cells: The Working Units of Life
text:
The first life on Earth was prokaryotic.

Prokaryotes are simple cells without a nucleus, like bacteria.

For about 1 billion years, only prokaryotes existed on Earth.
This period started when prokaryotic cells first appeared.
It lasted until about 2.7 billion years ago.
At 2.7 billion years ago, the first evidence of eukaryotic cells appears in ancient rocks.

Eukaryotes are complex cells with a nucleus – the ancestors of plants and animals.

A single prokaryotic cell is often biochemically specialized, limited in the resources it can use and the functions it can perform.



theory: the endomembrane system and the cell nucleus originated by related processes
A bacterium with enclosed compartments would have several evolutionary advantages.
Chemicals could be concentrated in particular regions of the cell, allowing chemical reactions to proceed more efficiently.
A biochemical process could be segregated within an organelle with, for example, a different pH from the rest of the cell, creating more favorable conditions for that process.
DNA transcription could be separated from translation, providing more opportunities for separate control of these steps in gene expression.





Symbiosis 共生 means “living together,” and often refers to two organisms that coexist, each one supplying something that the other needs.
theory of endosymbiosis: some organelles—mitochondria & plastids—arose not by an infolding of the cell membrane, but by one cell ingesting (but not digesting) another cell, giving rise to a symbiotic relationship.
Eventually, the ingested cell lost its autonomy and some of its functions.
Many of the ingested cell’s genes were transferred to the host’s DNA.
Mitochondria and plastids in today’s eukaryotic cells are the remnants of these symbionts, retaining some specialized function that benefit their host cells.
plastid:

About 2.5 billion years ago some prokaryotes (the cyanobacteria) developed photosynthesis.
The emergence of these prokaryotes was a key event in the evolution of complex organisms because they increased the \(\ce{O2}\) concentration in Earth’s atmosphere.
Plastids may have arisen by a similar event involving an ancestral eukaryote and a cyanobacterium 藻青菌.

Cells without cell walls can engulf relatively large particles by phagocytosis 吞噬作用.

e.g. phagocytes 吞噬细胞 in the human immune system, the engulfed particle can be an entire cell, such as a bacterium

title: Chapter 5 Cells: The Working Units of Life
text:
Cell theory:

Cells are the fundamental units of life.
All living organisms are composed of cells.
All cells come from preexisting cells.
Modern cells evolved from a common ancestor.

3 important implications of cell theory:

Studying cell biology is in some sense the same as studying life.
Life is continuous.
The origin of life on Earth was marked by the origin of the first cells.

acts as a selectively permeable barrier:

prevent some substances from crossing in
permit other substances to enter & leave the cell

regulate transport across it \(\Rightarrow\) allows the cell to maintain a more or less constant internal environment
important in

communicating with adjacent cells
receiving signals from the environment


Everything inside the cell, except for the nucleus if the cell has one, is termed the cytoplasm.
The cytosol is the fluid cytoplasm not contained inside another compartment.
prokaryote: organisms in Archaea and Bacteria

does not have membrane-enclosed internal compartments
does not have a nucleus

eukaryote: protists 原生生物, plants, fungi, and animals

contain membrane-enclosed comaprtments called organelles

nucleus:

where most of the cell’s DNA is located
where gene expression begins

title: Chapter 5 Cells: The Working Units of Life
text:
nucleus:

location of most of the cell’s DNA and the site of DNA replication
the site where gene transcription is turned on or off
nucleolus: a region within the nucleus

where ribosomes begin to be assembled from RNA and proteins


the nucleus is enclosed by nuclear envelope: an integrated structure composed of two membranes
chromosomes: long, thin threads

made up by chromatin: inside nucleus, DNA molecule + proteins

endomembrane system: interconnected system of membrane-enclosed compartments, includes:

cell membrane
nuclear envelope
endoplasmic reticulum 内质网
Golgi apparatus [细胞] 高尔基氏体; 内网器
lysosomes 溶酶体

vesicles 囊: membrane-surrounded droplets

shuttle substances between the various components of the endomembrane system

endoplasmic reticulum (ER) 内质网: networks of interconnected membranes branching throughout the cytoplasm

forming tubes and flattened sacs

rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) 带有核糖体的内质网: many ribosomes attached to the outer surface of the membrane, giving it a “rough” appearance in electron microscopy

receives into its lumen 内腔 (管状器官内的空腔) certain newly synthesized proteins

segregating them away from the cytoplasm
participates in transporting these proteins to other locations in the cell

proteins can be

chemically modified to alter their functions
“tag” them for delivery to specific cellular destinations

proteins are sent to destinations elsewhere in the cell enclosed within vesicles that pinch off from the RER
most membrane-bound proteins are made in the RER
glycoproteins 糖蛋白: some proteins become covalently linked to carbohydrate groups in the RER

smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) 平滑内质网: lacks ribosomes and is more tubular (and less like fattened sacs) than the RER, but shows continuity with portions of the RER

responsible for the chemical modification of small molecules taken in by the cell that may be toxic to the cell

make the targeted molecules more polar, so they are more water soluble and easily removed

is the site for glycogen degradation in animal cells
where lipids and steroids are synthesized, as well as some polysaccharides 多糖 in plant cells
store calcium ions, released trigger numerous cell responses

Golgi apparatus 内网器, consists of two components: flattened membranous sacs called cisternae 潴泡 (singular cisterna) that are piled up like saucers, and small membrane-enclosed vesicles

receives protein-containing vesicles from the RER
modifies, concentrates, packages, and sorts proteins. before they are sent to their cellular or extracellular destinations
adds carbohydrates to proteins
modifies other carbohydrates that were attached to proteins in the RER
where some polysaccharides for the plant cell wall are synthesized
cuts certain large precursor proteins transferred from the RER into smaller, functional fragments

3 functionally distinct regions (faces) of Golgi apparatus:

The cis face lies nearest to the nucleus or a patch of RER
The trans face lies closest to the cell membrane
The medial face lies in between

primary lysosomes: originate from the Golgi apoparatus
contain digestive enzymes
the sites where macromolecules (protein, polysaccharides, nucleic acids, lipids) are hydrolyzed into their monomers
phagocytosis 吞噬作用: a process of food, other cells, or foreign objects enter the cell
secondary lysosome [细胞][免疫] 次级溶酶体: phagosome 吞噬体 fuses with a primary lysosome to form a ~

where digestion occurs
there reactions are enhanced by the acidity of the lysosome’s interior

exocytosis (细胞生物学) 胞吐作用:

the “used” secondary lysosome containing undigested particles
moves to the cell membrane
fuses with it, and releases the undigested contents to the environment

autophagy (生物学) 自噬: programmed destruction of cell components

some cell components are continually being broken down and replaced by new ones

lysosomes 溶酶体:

where the cell breaks down its own materials
with the proper signal, lysosomes can engulf entire organelles, hydrolyzing their constituents

lysosomal storage diseases: caused by the failure of lysosomes to digest specific cellular components

invariably harmful or fatal
e.g. Tay-Sachs disease 黑蒙性家族性痴愚; 泰-萨二氏病

a particular lipid called a ganglioside [生化] 神经节苷脂 is not broken down in the lysosomes
instead accumulates in brain cells
a baby starts exhibiting neurological symptoms and becomes blind, deaf, and unable to swallow after 6 months of age
death occurs before age 4


plant cells do not appear to contain lysosomes, but the vacuole [细胞] 液泡 of a plant cell may function in an equivalent capacity because it, like lysosomes, hydrolyzes macromolecules
energy is harvested from

fuel molecules in the mitochondria 线粒体 (mitochondrion 的复数)

found in all eukaryotic cells

sunlight in the chloroplasts 叶绿体 of plant cells\

energy in biological systems is stored and transferred in the form of covalent bonds in organic molecules
In eukaryotic cells, breakdown of energy-rich molecules sucha s glucose begins in the cytoplasm.
mitochondria:

harvests the chemical-bond energy of those molecules in a form that he cell can use
namely the energy-rich molecule ATP (adenosine triphosphate 腺苷三磷酸)
some can reproduce and divide independently of the central nucleus
Cells that are active in movement and growth require the most chemical-bond energy and tend to have the most mitochondria.

cellular respiration

production of ATP in the mitochondria
using fuel molecules and molecular oxygen (\(\ce{O2}\))

Mitochondria have two membranes:

outer membrane:

smooth
permits the movement of substances into and out of the organelle

inner membrane:

folds inward in many places
has a surface area much greater tha nthat of the outer membrane
cristae 脊: shelflike structures
exerts much more control over what enters and leaves the space it encloses than does the outer membrane

large protein complexes embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane

participate tin cellular respiration


mitochondrial matrix 线粒体基质

the space enclosed by the inner membrane
contains ribosomes and DNA that are used to make some of the mitochondrial proteins needed for cellular respiration

plastids 质体，色素体:

occur only in the cells of plants and certain protists
can divide independently of the cell nucleus

chloroplasts 叶绿体: \(\nwarrow\) (one type of plastids)

contain the green pigment chlorophyll 叶绿素
are the sites of photosynthesis

light energy is converted into chemical-bond energy

enclosed by two membranes
thylakoids 类囊体: a series of internal membrane that often look like stacks of flat, hollow pita bread

only 10% are phospholipids 磷脂
the rest are galactose-substituted diglycerides 半乳糖取代的二甘油酯 and sulfolipids 硫脂
are the most abundant lipids in the biosphere
the membranes of the thylakoids contain chlorophyll and other pigments taht harvest light energy for photosynthesis

The thylakoids of one granum may be connected to those of other grana, making the interior of the chloroplast a highly developed network, much like the ER.
stroma 间质: the fluid in which the grana are suspended

contains ribosomes nad DNA

used to synthasize some chloroplast polypeptides



chromoplast 色素母细胞 (another type of plastids)

make and store red, yellow, and orange pigments
especially in flowers and fruits

leucoplasts [植] 白色体 (another type of plastids):

storage organelles that store starch

3 other organelles whose boundary membranes separate their specialized chemical reactions and contents from the rest fo the cytoplasm: peroxisomes 过氧物酶体, glyoxysomes 糖体, and vacuoles 液泡.
peroxisome 过氧物酶体:

found only in plants
organelles that accumulate toxic peroxides

e.g. hydrogen peroxide (\(\ce{H2O2}\)): occur as byproducts of some biochemical reactions
safely broken down inside the peroxisomes without mixing with other parts of the cell
\[\ce{RH2 + O2 -> R + H2O2 \text{(cellular reactions)}} \\
\ce{2H2O2 -> 2H2O + O2 \text{(inside peroxisome)}}\]


glyoxysome 糖体:

found only in plants
most abundant in young plants
they are the locations where stored lipids are converted into carbohydrates for transport to growing cells
The direct conversion of fat to carbohydrate is unique to these plants.

vacuole 液泡:

occur in many eukaryotic cells but particularly those of plants, fungi, and protists
arise from the ER or Golgi apparatus
structure:

in many plant cells, ~ take up more than 90% of the cell volume
grow as the cell grows
presence of dissolved substances in the vacuole causes water to enter it from the cytosol, making the vacuole swell like a balloon
A mature plant cell does not swell when the vacuole fills with water, since it has a rigid cell wall.
Instead, it stiffens 绷紧 from the increase in water pressure (called turgor (细胞组织的) 肿胀), and this supports the plant body.

reproduction:

~ contains some fo the pigments (especially blue and pink) in the petals and fruits of flowering plants
these pigments – the anthocyanins 花色素苷 – are visual cues that help attract animals that assist in pollination or seed dispersal

digestion:

in some plants, ~ in seeds contain molecules that hydrolyze stored proteins into monomers
during seed germination 发芽, the monomers are used as food by the developing plant seedlings

storage:

storing water
store toxic molecules and waste products
they may be poisonous or distasteful, these stored materials deter some animals from eating the plants and contribute to plant defense and survival
e.g. tannins 单宁酸: a class of polyphenols 多元酚 (具有抗氧化作用), made in many plants; in tea and red wine

bitter taste deters predators
dark color acts like animal melanin 黑色素 to protect the plant from ultraviolet light dmg
made in the chloroplast and end up in the vacuole
A newly disc9overed organelle, named tannosome 单宁体, contains tannins.



cytoskeleton 细胞骨架:

supports the cell and maintains its shape
holds cell organelles and other particles in position within the cell
moves organelles and other particles around in the cell
involved with movements of the cytoplasm, called cytoplasmic streaming 细胞质流动
interacts with extracellular structures, helping anchor 锚 the cell in place

microfilaments 微丝:

can exist as single filaments, in bundles, or in networks
about \(\pu{7nm}\) in diameter and up to several micrometers long
two major roles:

helpo the entire cell or parts of the cell move
determine and stabilize cell shape

assembled from monomers of actin 肌动蛋白: a protein that exists in several forms; has many function, especially in animals

has distinct ends: designated “plus” and “minus”
these ends permit actin monomers to interact with one another to form long, double-helical chains
the polymerization of actin into microfilaments is reversible
the microfilaments can disappear from cells by breaking down into monomers of free actin
Special actin-binding proteins mediate these processes.
in non-muscle cells, ~ filaments are associated with localized changes in cell shape

e.g. cytoplasmic streaming: flowing movement of the cytoplasm
e.g. amoeboid movement [细胞] 变形运动
e.g. “pinching” contractions that divide an animal cell into two daughter cells

involved in the formation of cellular extensions called pseudopodia 伪足: enables some cells to move


intermediate filaments 中间纤维

at least 50 different kinds
generally fall into six molecular classes that share the same general structure
one of these classes consists of fibrous proteins fo the keratin family, which also includes the proteins that make up hair and fingernails
tough, ropelike protein structures \(\pu{8-12nm}\) in diametere
more permanet tthatn the other two types in that they do not continually form and re-form
two major structural functions:

anchor cell structures in place

radiate from the nuclear envelope and help maintain the position of the nucleus and other organelles in the cell

resist tension

maintian rigidity in body surface tissues by stretching through the cytoplasm
connecting specialized membrane structures called desmosomes 细胞桥粒 (上皮细胞膜中的局部增厚部份)



microtubules 微管: long, hollow, unbranched cylinders about \(\pu{25nm}\) in diameter and up to several micrometers long

two roles in the cell:

form a rigid internal skeleton for some cells
act as a framework along which motor proteins can move structures within the cell

Microtubule = chain of dimers
dimer 二聚物 = \(\alpha\)-tubulin 微管蛋白 + \(\beta\)-tubulin (paired)
\(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) = two similar proteins
One dimer → next dimer → tube grows
Thirteen chains of tubulin doublets surround the central cavity of hte microtubule.
\[\ce{\alpha-tubulin + \beta-tubulin -> \alpha\beta doublet -> polymer of doublets (microtubule)}\]
the two ends of a microtubule are different: one is designated the “plus” end and the other the “minus” end.
Tubulin dimers can be rapidly added or subtracted, mainly at the plus end, lengthening or shortening the microtubule.
\[\text{Microtubules} \leftrightarrow \text{tubulin doublets}\]
The capacity to change length rapidly makes microtubules dynamic structures: they are readily adapted for new purposes in the cell.
e.g. by disassembly 分解 and reassembly 重组, they can drag along substances attached to them
In plants, microtubules act as a framework for the assembly of cellulose and help orient the cellulose fibers of the cell wall.

motor proteins: specialized molecules that use cellular energy to change their shapes and move

bind to and move along the microtubules, carrying materials from one part of the cell to another
two main types of motor proteins:

kinesins 驱动蛋白: move materials toward the “plus” end
dyneins 动力蛋白: move materials toward the “minus” end


microtubules and their associated proteins line the interior of cilia 纤毛 and flagella 鞭毛 on eukaryotic cells

many cells have one or the other of these appendages, which form from projections of the cell membrane

cilia: \(\pu{0.25\mu m}\) in length

They occur by the hundreds on individual cells and move stiffly to either propel the cell (i.e. in protists 原生生物) or to move fluid over a stationary cell (i.e. in the human respiratory system)

flagella: longer, \(\pu{100}\) to \(\pu{200\mu m}\)

occur singly or in pairs
can push or pull a cell through its aqueous environment

In cell biology, two approaches are often used to show that a structure or process A causes function B:

Inhibition: Use a drug thta inhibits A and see if B still occurs. If it does not, then A is probably a causative factor for B.
Mutation: Examine a cell that lacks the gene (or genes) for A and see if B still occurs. If it does not, then A is probably a causative factor for B.

title: Chapter 6 Cell Membranes
text:
fluid mosaic model 流动镶嵌模型: the phospholipid bilayer serves as a lipid “lake” in which a variety of proteins “float”

“mosaid” because it is made up of many discrete components
“fluid” because components can move freely





the major lipid components of biological membranes


phospholipids:

form thin bilayers
with their charged, hydrophilic “heads” on the external surface interacting with the aqueous environment
nonpolar, fatty acid “tails” interacting with each other on the inside of hte membrane

thickness of a biological membrane is about 8nm ($ $), about 2 times of a phospholid $ $ bilayer
membranes from different organelles within a cell may vary greatly in their lipid composition, e.g., differ in:

fatty acid chain length (number of carbon atoms)
degree of unsaturation (number of double bonds) in the fatty acids
the polar groups present





The Fluid Mosaic ModelThe general molecular structure of a biological membran eis a continuous phospholipid bilayer that has proteins embeded in or associated wiht it.



Anchored membrane proteins are covalently bonded to lipids that are inserted into the membrane.
Cholesterol 胆固醇 alters membrane fluidity

The saturated chains allow close packing of fatty acids in the bilayer.
The “kinks” 扭结 in unsaturated fatty acids make for a less dense, more fluid packing.

The steroid cholesterol 类固醇 is an abundant component (20%-50%) of animal cell membranes.

The hydroxyl group of cholesterol interacts with the polar eneds of phospholipids, and the nonpolar rings and hydrocarbon chain insert into the fatty acids chains in the interior of the membrane.
Cholesterol is important for membrane integrity 完整性 and modulates membrane fluidity.
The cholestrol in your membranes is not hazardous 有害的 to your health.








Note



胆固醇本身无问题，但位置和运输方式很重要。

在 cell membrane 里， 正常 & 必须
在血液里，不溶于水，必须搭乘 lipoproteins 脂蛋白运输

LDL “bad cholesterol”
HDL “good cholesterol”

LDL \(\Uparrow\), 容易把胆固醇沉积到血管壁

时间 \(\Uparrow\), atherosclerotic plaques 动脉粥样硬化斑块





Since spontaneous phospholipid flip-flops are rare, the inner and outer halves of the bilayer may be quite different in the kinds of phospholipids they contain.
2 particularly important factors affects membrane fluidity:

Lipid composition:


Cholesterol and long-chain, saturated fatty acids, pack tightly beside on another, with little room for movement
This close packing results in less fluid membranes.
A membrane with shorter-chain fatty acids, unsaturated fatty acids, or less cholesterol is more fluid.


Temperature


At \(\Downarrow\) Temperature, molecuels move more slowly and fluidity decreases at reduced temperatures \(\Longrightarrow\) cellular processes that take place within the membrane may slow down or stop under cold conditions in organisms that cannot keep their bodies warm.
In some organisms the lipid composition of their membranes changes when they get cold, replacing saturated with unsaturated fatty acids and using fatty acids with shorter tails.
Theses changes play a role in the survival of plants, bacteria, and hibernating animals during the winter.






a modified cell membrane that encloses portions of some neurons (nerve cells) and acts as an electrical insulator

myelin has only 1 protein for every 70 lipids



About \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the protein-coding genes in the eukaryotic genome encode membrane proteins.


一种永久附着在生物膜上的蛋白质（或蛋白组装体）


Integral membrane proteins 整合膜蛋白 are at least partly embedded in the phospholipid bilayer.
Integral membranes proteins have both hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions (domains)

hydrophilic domains 亲水区:

stretches of amino acids with hydrophilic side chains (R groups) give certain regions of the protein a polar character
interact with water
stick out into the aqueous environment inside or outside the cell or organelle

hydrophobic domains 恐水区:

stretches of amino acids with hydrophobic side chains give other regions of the protein a nonpolar character
interact with the fatty acids in the interior of hte phospholipid bilayer, away from water





一类与细胞膜表面相互作用的蛋白质，不像跨膜蛋白那样穿过脂质双层，而是通过与脂质双层或其他膜蛋白的相互作用而附在膜上。


Peripheral membrane proteins 周边膜蛋白 lack exposed hydrophobic groups.

not embedded in the bilayer
have polar or charged regions that interact with

exposed parts of integral membrane proteins
or with the polar heads of phospholipid molecules


Anchored membrane protein 锚定膜蛋白 are covalently attached to fatty acids or other lipid groups.

The hydrophobic lipid groups insert into the phospholipid bilayer and hold these proteins in association with the membrane.



an integral protein that extends all the way through the phospholipid bilayer and protrudes on both sides


In addition to having one or more transmembrane domains 跨膜区 that extends all the way through the bilayer such a protein may have domains with other specific functions on the inner and outer sides of the membrane.
Peripheral membrane proteins, by contrast, are located on one side of the membrane or the other.



This asymmetrical arrangement of membrane proteins gives the two surfaces of the membrane different properties.



some membrane proteins move around relatively freely within the phospholipid bilayer
some proteins confined to a specific region of the membrane

e.g., like animals at a zoo: the animals are free to move around within the fenced area, but not outside it







There are major chemical differences amoung the membranes of even a single eukaryotic cell.





A glycolipid 糖脂类 consists of a carbohydrate covalently bonded to a lipid.

Extending out from the cell surface, the carbohydrate may serve as a recognition signal for interactions between cells.
e.g. The carbohydrates on some glycolipids change when cells become cancerous. This change may allow white blood cells to target cancer cells for destruction.

A glycoprotein 糖蛋白 consists of one or more short carbohydrate chains covalently bonded to a protein.

The bound carbohydrates are oligosaccharides 寡糖, 低聚糖, usually not exceeding 20 monosaccharide units in length.
A proteoglycan 蛋白多糖 is a more heavily glycosylated 糖基化 protein 蛋白

it has more carbohydrate molecules attached to it
the carbohydrate chains are often longer than they are in glycoproteins.


The carbohydrates of glycoproteins and proteoglycans often function in cell recognitnion and adhesion.



Glycoprotein = 糖化蛋: 主体是 protein, 上面挂了一些短的 carbohydrate chains
Proteoglycan = 蛋化糖: 主体看起来更像一大坨 carbohydrate, 只有一个 protein core, 上面挂着大量超长的 GAG (glycosaminoglycan) chains




How do the hydrophobic and hydrophilic regions of phospholipids form a membrane bilayer?


Hydrophilic heads face the watery environments inside and outside the cell, while hydrophobiic tails point inward away fro mwater, forming a bilayer.


What differentiates an integral protein from a peripheral protein?


integral proteins are embedded in or span the membrane
peripheral protein are loosely attached to the membrane surface


If a cell membrane is frozen and then fractured so that the two leaflets of the cell membrane are peeled away from each other, bumps appear in electron microscopy. What are the bumps?


The bumps are integral membrane proteins embedded within the lipid bilayer.


When a normal lung cell becomes a lung cancer cell, there are several important changes in cell membrane properties. How would you investigate the observation that the cancer cell membrane is more fluid, with more rapid diffusion in the plane of the membrane of both lipids and proteins?


Use FRAP (fluorescence recovery after photobleaching).
Label membrane lipids or proteins with fluorescent markers, bleach a small region with a laser, and measure how quickly fluorescence returns.
Faster recovery in cancer cells would indicate faster lateral diffusion and therefore greater membrane fluidity.

form thin bilayers

nonpolar, fatty acid “tails” interacting with each other on the inside of hte membrane

the polar groups present

The saturated chains allow close packing of fatty acids in the bilayer.

胆固醇本身无问题，但位置和运输方式很重要。

在 cell membrane 里， 正常 & 必须

LDL “bad cholesterol”

Lipid composition:


Cholesterol and long-chain, saturated fatty acids, pack tightly beside on another, with little room for movement
This close packing results in less fluid membranes.

At \(\Downarrow\) Temperature, molecuels move more slowly and fluidity decreases at reduced temperatures \(\Longrightarrow\) cellular processes that take place within the membrane may slow down or stop under cold conditions in organisms that cannot keep their bodies warm.

a modified cell membrane that encloses portions of some neurons (nerve cells) and acts as an electrical insulator

myelin has only 1 protein for every 70 lipids

一种永久附着在生物膜上的蛋白质（或蛋白组装体）

hydrophilic domains 亲水区:

stretches of amino acids with hydrophilic side chains (R groups) give certain regions of the protein a polar character
interact with water
stick out into the aqueous environment inside or outside the cell or organelle

hydrophobic domains 恐水区:

stretches of amino acids with hydrophobic side chains give other regions of the protein a nonpolar character
interact with the fatty acids in the interior of hte phospholipid bilayer, away from water





一类与细胞膜表面相互作用的蛋白质，不像跨膜蛋白那样穿过脂质双层，而是通过与脂质双层或其他膜蛋白的相互作用而附在膜上。


Peripheral membrane proteins 周边膜蛋白 lack exposed hydrophobic groups.

not embedded in the bilayer
have polar or charged regions that interact with

exposed parts of integral membrane proteins
or with the polar heads of phospholipid molecules


Anchored membrane protein 锚定膜蛋白 are covalently attached to fatty acids or other lipid groups.

The hydrophobic lipid groups insert into the phospholipid bilayer and hold these proteins in association with the membrane.



an integral protein that extends all the way through the phospholipid bilayer and protrudes on both sides


In addition to having one or more transmembrane domains 跨膜区 that extends all the way through the bilayer such a protein may have domains with other specific functions on the inner and outer sides of the membrane.
Peripheral membrane proteins, by contrast, are located on one side of the membrane or the other.



This asymmetrical arrangement of membrane proteins gives the two surfaces of the membrane different properties.



some membrane proteins move around relatively freely within the phospholipid bilayer
some proteins confined to a specific region of the membrane

e.g., like animals at a zoo: the animals are free to move around within the fenced area, but not outside it







There are major chemical differences amoung the membranes of even a single eukaryotic cell.





A glycolipid 糖脂类 consists of a carbohydrate covalently bonded to a lipid.

Extending out from the cell surface, the carbohydrate may serve as a recognition signal for interactions between cells.
e.g. The carbohydrates on some glycolipids change when cells become cancerous. This change may allow white blood cells to target cancer cells for destruction.

A glycoprotein 糖蛋白 consists of one or more short carbohydrate chains covalently bonded to a protein.

The bound carbohydrates are oligosaccharides 寡糖, 低聚糖, usually not exceeding 20 monosaccharide units in length.
A proteoglycan 蛋白多糖 is a more heavily glycosylated 糖基化 protein 蛋白

it has more carbohydrate molecules attached to it
the carbohydrate chains are often longer than they are in glycoproteins.


The carbohydrates of glycoproteins and proteoglycans often function in cell recognitnion and adhesion.



Glycoprotein = 糖化蛋: 主体是 protein, 上面挂了一些短的 carbohydrate chains
Proteoglycan = 蛋化糖: 主体看起来更像一大坨 carbohydrate, 只有一个 protein core, 上面挂着大量超长的 GAG (glycosaminoglycan) chains




How do the hydrophobic and hydrophilic regions of phospholipids form a membrane bilayer?


Hydrophilic heads face the watery environments inside and outside the cell, while hydrophobiic tails point inward away fro mwater, forming a bilayer.


What differentiates an integral protein from a peripheral protein?


integral proteins are embedded in or span the membrane
peripheral protein are loosely attached to the membrane surface


If a cell membrane is frozen and then fractured so that the two leaflets of the cell membrane are peeled away from each other, bumps appear in electron microscopy. What are the bumps?


The bumps are integral membrane proteins embedded within the lipid bilayer.


When a normal lung cell becomes a lung cancer cell, there are several important changes in cell membrane properties. How would you investigate the observation that the cancer cell membrane is more fluid, with more rapid diffusion in the plane of the membrane of both lipids and proteins?


Use FRAP (fluorescence recovery after photobleaching).
Label membrane lipids or proteins with fluorescent markers, bleach a small region with a laser, and measure how quickly fluorescence returns.
Faster recovery in cancer cells would indicate faster lateral diffusion and therefore greater membrane fluidity.

Large molecules enter and leave a cell through vesicles.








phospholipid bilayer: hydrophilic heads face outward, hydrophobic tails face inward.
fluid mosaic model: proteins float in or on the lipid bilayer.





Phospholipids vary in chain length, saturation, and polar groups.
Cholesterol modulates membrane fluidity and stability.

Lipid composition (saturated vs unsaturated fatty acids)

saturated = \(\Downarrow\) fluidity
unsaturated = \(\Uparrow\) fluidity

Temperature

\(\Downarrow\) T = \(\Downarrow\) fluidity
\(\Uparrow\) T = \(\Uparrow\) fluidity

integral proteins: embedded in bilayer, have hydrophilic and hydrophobic domains
peripheral proteins: bound to membrane surface, no hydrophobic domains

Cell fusion experiments show proteins can diffuse laterally.
Cytoskeleton can restrict protein movement.





Membranes are constantly forming, fusing, and recycling via vesicles.
Different organelles have different membrane compositions.

Carbohydrate structures provide diverse recognition signals.

Sponge cell experiments show species-specific recognition.





Proteoglycans with sulfated polysaccharides mediate recognition and binding.

tight junction 紧密连接: seal intercellular spaces
desmosome 细胞桥粒: provide mechanical strength
gap junction 间隙连接: allow communication via channels





integrins 整联蛋白 connect ECM to cytoskeleton and enable cell movement









Net movememnt from high to low concentration
rate depends on

molecular size / mass (\(\mathrm{m}\))
temperature (\(\mathrm{T}\))
solution density (\(\rho\))
concentration gradient (\(\frac{\mathrm{d}c}{\mathrm{d}x}\))
surface area and distance (\(\mathrm{A}\) and \(\mathrm{d}\))







Small, hydrophobic molecules pass directly through the bilayer.
Polar/charged molecules diffuse poorly.






Water moves toward higher solute concentration.
Terms:

isotonic 等渗的: equal solute concentrations
hypotonic 低渗的: lower solute outside \(\Longrightarrow\) water enters cell
hypertonic 高渗的: higher solute outside \(\Longrightarrow\) water leaves cell

渗透压: 植物细胞内液体由于渗入作用而产生的实际压力, 与具有相同浓度的液体在理论上可能产生的最大压力相对比。






channel proteins 离子通道蛋白 form hydrophilic pores

离子通道蛋白: 一种成孔蛋白, 通过允许特定类型的离子穿过通道来帮助细胞建立和控制质膜间的微弱电压差
e.g., ion channels, aquaporins 水通道蛋白, 水孔蛋白

carrier proteins 载体蛋白 bind substances and change shape

载体蛋白: 一种功能是通过生物膜运输小分子(或其他蛋白质)的蛋白质
e.g., glucose transporter










moves substances against concentration / electrical gradients
requries energy (usually ATP)





uniporter 单向传递体: moves one substance one way
symporter 协同载体: moves two substances same direction
antiporter 反向转运体: moves two substances opposite directions





direct use of ATP
e.g., \(\ce{Na+ - K+}\) pump

3 \(\ce{Na+}\) out, 2 \(\ce{K+}\) in
\(\ce{ATP -> ADP + P_i}\)






Uses energy from ion gradient (established by primary transport)
e.g., \(\ce{Na+ - glucose}\) symporter in intestinal cells 肠道细胞
applied in oral rehydration therapy (ORT) 口服补液疗法









phagocytosis 吞噬作用 (“cell eating”): large particles or cells
pinocytosis 胞饮作用 (“cell drinking”): fluids and dissolved substances
receptor-mediated endocytosis 受体介导的内吞作用: specific uptake via receptor proteins in coated pits

一种细胞摄取特定物质的过程, 通过特定的受体与物质结合, 然后将受体与物质一起内化到细胞内部
e.g., LDL cholesterol 低密度脂蛋白胆固醇 uptake






vesicles fuse with cell membrane to release contents
e.g., neurotransmitter release 神经递质释放

神经元通过释放神经递质来传递信号的过程

e.g., sweat secretion

water channels that allow rapid, selective water movement
important in kidneys, plant roots, and vacuoles
can be regulated (gated) in response to environmental conditions
potential applications: water purification, desalination 海水淡化, cosmetics

title: Chapter 7: Cell Communication and Multicellularity
text:
a sequence of molecular events and chemical reactions that lead to a cell’s response to a signal
every pathway involves three elements

signal 信号
receptor 受体
response 响应












Signal Type
Mode of Action
Example




autocrine 自分泌
diffuse to and affect the cells that produce them
tumor cells that make and respond to signals stimulating cell division


juxtacrine 领分泌/接触依赖
affect only cells right next to and in contact with the signal-producing cell
common during development when cells are differentiating


paracrine 旁分泌
diffuse to and affect nearby cells
inflammation signals from skin cells to nearby blood cells during healing


hormones 激素
travel through circulatory systems of animals or vascular system of plants
signals that act on distant cells







All cells may be exposed to a signal, but only cells with the appropriate receptors can respond.
Specificity depends on whether the target cell expresses the specific receptor for that signal.





Interactions between different signal transduction 传导 pathways.
Multiple pathways may converge on a single transcription factor, allowing a single gene to be regulated by multiple signals.
Activation of one pathway may inhibit another.
Biologists often refer to “signaling networks 信号网络” rather than pathways due to this complexity.









A specific chemical signal molecule that fits into a 3-D site on its protein receptor.
Ligand binding causes the receptor protein to undergo a conformational change 构想变化, initiating a cellular response.
The ligand itself is usually not changed; its role is purely to “knock on the door” 触发信号.





binding is reversible:

\[
\ce{R + L <=> RL}
\]

rate of binding

\[
\ce{k_1[R][L]}
\]

rate of dissociation

\[
\ce{k_2[RL]}
\]

at equilibrium:

\[
\ce{k_1[R][L]} = \ce{k_2[RL]}
\]

Dissociation Constant 解离常数, \(\ce{K_D}\)

\[
\ce{K_D} = \frac{k_2}{k_1} = \frac{\ce{[R][L]}}{\ce{[RL]}}
\]
Lower \(\mathrm{K_D}\) = higher affinity 亲和力高 of ligand for receptor
Higher \(\mathrm{K_D}\) = lower affinity 亲和力低, more ligand needed to trigger signal transduction






agonists 激动剂: chemicals that bind to the receptor and set it into signal transduction mode, just like the ligand
antagonist 拮抗剂: inhibitors that bind to the receptor and “freeze” it in place, preventing the real ligand from binding, but do not trigger signal transduction



Caffeine has a structure similar to adenosine 腺苷
acts as an antagonist at adenosine receptors
preventing adenosine binding and allowing continued nerve cell activity.














Receptor Type
Location
Signals Detected
Example




membrane receptors 膜受体
cell membrane
large or polar ligands that cannot cross the lipid bilayer
insulin receptor 胰岛素受体


intracellular receptors 胞内受体
cytoplasm or nucleus
small or nonpolar ligands that can diffuse across the membrane
estrogen receptor 雌激素受体cortisol receptor 皮质醇受体







Ion Channels 离子通道受体


Ligand binding causes conformational change in the channel protein, opening the gate, allowing ions (\(\ce{Na+}\), \(\ce{K+}\), \(\ce{Ca^2+}\), \(\ce{Cl-}\)) to enter or leave the cell.



acetylcholine receptor:

a ligand-gated \(\ce{Na+}\) channel located in the cell membrane of skeletal muscle cells
composed of 5 polypeptide subunits
when acetylcholine binds to 2 of the subunits, the gate opens and \(\ce{Na+}\) flows into the cell, initiating muscle contraction




Protein Kinase Receptors 蛋白激酶受体


catalyze the phosphorylation 磷酸化 of themselves or other proteins, changing their shape and function
3 amino acids can be phosphorylated: serine 丝氨酸, threonine 苏氨酸, tyrosine 酪氨酸
over 500 genes encode protein kinases in humans



insuline receptor:

has 2 copies of \(\alpha\) subunits and 2 copies of \(\beta\) subunits
when insulin binds, the receptor becomes activated and phosphorylates itself and insulin-response substrates
the ultimately leads to insertion of glucose transporters 葡萄糖转运蛋白 into the cell membrane




G Protein-Coupled Receptors G蛋白偶联受体, GPCR


many roles

light detection (photoreceptors 光感受器)
odor detection (olfactory receptors 嗅觉受体)
regulation of mood and behavior (e.g., mating in voles)

the receptors for oxytocin 催产素 and vasopressin 加压素 are G protein-coupled receptors
structure: 3 polypeptide subunits (\(\alpha\), \(\beta\), \(\gamma\)); can bind receptor, GDP/GTP, and effector protein
mechanisms of aciton:

Ligand binds to extracellular side of receptor \(\Longrightarrow\) receptor changes shape
Cytoplasmic region exposes a site that binds to a G protein
G protein binds to activated receptor; GDP is exchanged for GTP
GTP-bound \(\alpha\) submit separates from the \(\beta \gamma\) subunits and diffuses in the membrane
\(\alpha\) submits binds to and activates and effector protein 效应蛋白
GTP is hydrolyzed to GDP \(\Longrightarrow\) \(\alpha\) subunit becomes inactive and reassembles with \(\beta \gamma\) subunits






located in the cytoplasm or nucleus
respond to physical signals (e.g., light) or chemical signals that can cross the cell membrane (e.g., steroid hormones)
many intracellular receptors are transcription factors 转录因子



normally bound to a chaperone protein 分子伴侣 that blocks it from entering the nucleus
cortisol binding causes the receptor to change shape, releasing the chaperone 分子伴侣
the receptor enters the nucleus and binds to DNA, altering gene transcription










e.g., Ras signaling pathway 肾素-血管紧张素系统（renin-angiotensin system） (Ras is a G protein)
pathway: growth factor \(\Longrightarrow\) receptor tyrosine kinase \(\Longrightarrow\) Ras (G protein) \(\Longrightarrow\) MAPK cascade \(\Longrightarrow\) nucleus \(\Longrightarrow\) gene expression \(\Longrightarrow\) cell division
Ras and cancer: In some bladder cancer cells, Ras is permanently bound to GTP and constantly active, causing continuous cell division





amplification 信号放大: each activated protein kinase can phosphorylate many target proteins
signal reaches the nucleus 信号传递到细胞核: membrane signals can affect gene expression
specificity 特异性: multiple steps provide more regulation levels
response diversity 响应多样性: different target proteins at each step can produce different effects


1 molecule of epinephrine 肾上腺素 binds to receptor on liver cell \(\Longrightarrow\)

activates 20 molecuels of cAMP \(\Longrightarrow\)
activates 20 molecules of protein kinase A \(\Longrightarrow\)
activates 100 molecles of phosphorylase kinase \(\Longrightarrow\)
activates 1,000 molecules of glycogen phosphorylase \(\Longrightarrow\)
produces 10,000 molecules of glucose-1-phosphate \(\Longrightarrow\)
releases 10,000 molecuels of blood glucose






Cyclic AMP 环磷酸腺苷 cAMP


produced from ATP by adenylyl cyclase 腺苷酸环化酶
broken down by phosphodiesterase 磷酸二酯酶
functions: amplifies signal, distributes signal to multiple targets
multiple receptors can use the same cAMP pathway to produce different effects


Lipid-Derived Second Messengers 脂质来源的第二信使


source: phosphatidyl inositol-bisphosphate 磷脂酰肌醇二磷酸 \(\ce{PIP2}\)
phospholipase C 磷脂酶 C, hydrolyzes \(\ce{PIP2}\) to produce:

\(\ce{IP3}\) 肌醇三磷酸, inositol trisphosphate: released into the cytoplasm; acts on \(\ce{Ca^2+}\) channels in the ER membrane

Laws of Thermodynamics 热力学定律

First Law of Thermodynamics

Second Law of Thermodynamics

Free Energy (G) 自由能

\[ \Delta \mathrm{G} = \Delta \mathrm{H} - \mathrm{T} \Delta \mathrm{S}\]

releases energy, spontaneous

\(\Delta \mathrm{G} > 0\): endergonic 吸能

requires energy input

\(\Delta \mathrm{G} = 0\): at equilibrium

no net change


Equilibrium 平衡

forward and reverse reactions occur at same rate
product-to-reactant ratio is fixed

\(\Delta \mathrm{G} \approx \pu{-7.3kcal/mol}\) \((\pu{-30kJ/mol})\), highly exergonic

Negative charges repel - bond is high-energy
Products (\(\ce{ADP + P_i}\)) are more stable

stored energy

e.g., concentration gradients

kinetic energy:

energy of movememt
does work


metabolism 新陈代谢

anabolism 合成代谢:

builds larger molecules
requires energy
endergonic 吸能的, \(+ \Delta \mathrm{G}\)

catabolism 分解代谢

breaks down larger molecules
releases energy
exergonic 放能的, \(- \Delta \mathrm{G}\)


Laws of Thermodynamics 热力学定律

First Law of Thermodynamics

Energy is neither created nor destroyed 能量守恒, only converted

Second Law of Thermodynamics

Energy conversions increase entropy 熵 (S) 无序度增加
some energy becomes unusable


Free Energy (G) 自由能

\[ \Delta \mathrm{G} = \Delta \mathrm{H} - \mathrm{T} \Delta \mathrm{S}\]
\(\Delta \mathrm{G} < 0\): exergonic 放能

releases energy, spontaneous

\(\Delta \mathrm{G} > 0\): endergonic 吸能

requires energy input

\(\Delta \mathrm{G} = 0\): at equilibrium

no net change


Equilibrium 平衡

forward and reverse reactions occur at same rate
product-to-reactant ratio is fixed

title: Chapter 8: Energy, Enzymes, and Metabolism
text:
Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP) 三磷酸腺苷

energy currency of the cell
structure:\[\text{adenine 腺嘌呤} + \text{ribose 核糖} + 3 \text{phosphate groups 磷酸基团}\]

ATP Hydrolysis ATP 水解

\[\ce{ATP + H2O -> ADP + P_i + free energy}\]
\(\Delta \mathrm{G} \approx \pu{-7.3kcal/mol}\) \((\pu{-30kJ/mol})\), highly exergonic
Why so much energy?

Negative charges repel - bond is high-energy
Products (\(\ce{ADP + P_i}\)) are more stable


Energy Coupling 能量偶联

ATP hydrolysis drives endergonic reactions
e.g.,\[\ce{Glucose + ATP -> Glucose-6-phosphate +ADP}\] 葡萄糖磷酸化
Cycle:\[\ce{Exergonic reactions -> make ATP}\]\[\ce{ATP -> fuels endergonic reactions}\]
